observations: A flat cyan figure stands in profile against a solid deep-red field, both arms extended forward at different heights, fingers spread and loosely drawn.
A tightly coiled yellow spiral sits where an eye would be on the head; a row of small yellow zigzag marks runs along the jaw, and a separate yellow zigzag band floats above the skull.
Dark red lines cut into the cyan body at the torso and hip, creating narrow gaps that read as divisions rather than shading.
reading: The cyan figure leans forward, arms reaching at uneven heights while the spiral eye and zigzag crown pull attention upward. The two-color field—deep red behind, flat cyan in front—keeps the form stark. Small yellow marks at jaw and crown add a nervous, almost rattling quality to what might otherwise read as a plain silhouette. The spread fingers on each hand differ, leaving the gesture open-ended.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #263 and nnxyz nnotb #265. All three share a flat figure-on-field structure, but the palette shifts across each: gold-on-crimson, red-on-deep-red, then pink-on-black.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #265 places a small spiral eye and zigzag crown on a flat figure against a dark field, making those specific marks directly comparable across both works.

Scrimshaw9 uses a tight coiled spiral as a focal mark near the face; the collector links nnxyz to scrimshaw through visual qualities, and this recurring coiled-line motif is a concrete point of contact.

lookingQuestion: The two arms reach at different heights with fingers spread differently on each hand—what does the difference in position between the upper and lower arm suggest about the figure's stance?
ambiguities: The dark-red lines cutting into the cyan torso could be body divisions, clothing seams, or background showing through; the image alone does not resolve this.
The Scrimshaw9 spiral comparison is meaningful as a repeated mark but the two works differ substantially in color density and line approach, making the connection narrow.
